maml:description.maml:para: Enables the everyday console views, native format commands and theme colours.

Three ways to use ConsoleMonster output: Automatic: enable formatting, then use ordinary commands for known and registered types. Explicit: pipe any objects to Show-ConsoleTable to choose columns, a title and grouping, or to Show-ConsoleObject to explore their members. These commands do not change session formatting; Show-ConsoleObject -StaticSnapshot avoids interactive input in scripts. Native Format commands: FormatCommands styles direct console output while keeping PowerShell's column choices; it is included by default; use -Exclude FormatCommands to leave it native. You do not need both automatic and explicit formatting. The -Feature parameter requires ConsoleMonster 2.1.0 or later.

By default, Output, FormatCommands, Errors, Streams and ReadLine are enabled. Format-Table, Format-List and Format-Wide keep PowerShell's column choices and change only direct console output; pipelines, captures, files, jobs, remoting and transcripts remain native. Use Include to add opt-in features and Exclude to remove features from the default set. Feature replaces the default set with exactly the selected features. Prompt, Help, Progress and GridView require Include or Feature. CompactErrors opts into the compact error layout. Get-ConsoleFormatting reports what is enabled. Disable-ConsoleFormatting restores the session.

Files, processes, services, structured records, commands, modules, history, IP addresses, volumes, versions, dictionaries and registered types get built-in or registered views. Explicit Show-Console commands remain available when you want to choose the view yourself. Custom Out-Default functions are kept unless Force is specified; Prompt does not replace oh-my-posh or Starship without Force.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs a console dashboard live while a script does the work.

The script runs in a runspace the module owns (or, with -Parallel, once per input item on a runspace pool, started as items arrive and limited by -ThrottleLimit). Inside it, $ConsoleSession, Update-Console and Write-ConsoleLogEntry update the screen; Write-Host, Write-Warning, Write-Verbose, errors and Console.WriteLine go to the dashboard's log region instead of scribbling over the screen. The screen is redrawn at about 15 frames per second however many updates arrive. Ctrl+C stops the script and always restores the terminal; the dashboard then leaves the alternate screen and prints its final state (or -Summary). Script output is returned when the dashboard ends. In redirected or CI output the dashboard becomes append-only lines. Variables and functions from the caller are not visible inside the script: read a variable with $using:name (as with ForEach-Object -Parallel), bring functions in with -ImportFunction, or pass values with -ArgumentList and a param() block.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs Pester tests with a live ConsoleMonster dashboard and a summary table.

Takes the parameters of Invoke-Pester (Path, ExcludePath, TagFilter, ExcludeTagFilter, FullNameFilter, Container, Output, CI, PassThru) or a -Configuration (a PesterConfiguration or a hashtable), and runs Pester 5 or 6, imported when first needed. While the tests run, an inline area (or the full screen with -FullScreen) shows the run totals and the clock, the test files as lanes with passed, failed and skipped counts, the running test, and with -FullScreen the failures (expected against actual, the file and line as a link), the slowest tests and a histogram of durations. When the run ends a table of results by file, the failures and the totals are written to the scrollback, and -ExportHtml saves the final dashboard. In redirected output, jobs and CI logs the output is one line per failure and a summary line. Pester's result object is returned with -PassThru (or Run.PassThru), Run.Throw and Run.Exit (-CI) are applied after the summary, and Write-Host output from tests appears above the inline area. Pester has no public reporter API, so the live view uses Pester's internal plugin steps through a guarded adapter; when the internals are not what it expects (or with Run.Parallel or Output None) Pester runs unchanged with its own output and the summary table follows. Works on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs a script block for every input item, optionally in parallel, with a live view of the run.

$_ is the item, as in ForEach-Object. While it runs, a live view shows a summary line (done of total, percentage, time left, counts), one cell per item, the running items with their elapsed time and the failures; without an interactive console (redirected output, CI, a job) it prints one line per finished item and a summary instead. The output is the script block's ordinary output, in input order (or as each item finishes with -Unordered); an item's errors are written as error records and mark it as failed. While the live view is showing, ordinary output and native stream records are delivered when it ends. With -Parallel, while the live view is showing, host messages, warnings, information, verbose and debug messages, and errors also appear immediately in its log; Write-Progress appears in an activity list, with independent parent and child activities per worker. Without -Parallel, progress bars from the script block are hidden while the live view is showing. Without -Parallel the items run one at a time in the caller's scope, as with ForEach-Object, so variables set in the script block stay. -Parallel runs up to -ThrottleLimit items at a time in their own runspaces on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7: variables of the caller are passed with $using:name, and -TimeoutSeconds stops an item that runs too long. -Label sets each item's label: a property name or a script block. -RetryCount runs a failed or timed-out item again (after -RetryDelaySeconds); only the last attempt's output and errors are kept, the item's cell shows the retry and the summary counts retried items. Ctrl+C stops the run: running items are stopped and the rest are counted as skipped.

maml:description.maml:para: Creates a run clock (ConsoleMonster.Live.SimulatedClock) the script moves forward, for simulated runs whose screen shows simulated time.

A live session reads the clock for the header clock, the summary bar's elapsed time and time left, the times of log lines and activities, and the run result's duration, so a demo or a replay of logged work shows its own time instead of the wall clock. Give it to a menu run as the third argument of $MenuContext.Run($dashboard, { ... }, $clock), or to Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -Clock. In the script, $clock.Wait(seconds) and $clock.WaitUntil(seconds) move it forward in small steps, sleeping 1/-Speed of each simulated second (never at speed 0, which runs at once); $clock.Advance(seconds) jumps without waiting and $clock.Hold(seconds) waits real time with the clock standing still. $clock.Elapsed is the time on the clock. Once the dashboard is stopped (Ctrl+C) waits stop sleeping, so the script reaches its end at once.

Foreground colour per piece: ConsoleColor names (exactly as Write-Host shows them: DarkRed is ANSI red, Red bright red; grey spells Gray), theme roles, #RRGGBB, rgb(r,g,b), r,g,b, or a markup palette name (cadetblue; palette.darkred for the palette colour where the bare name is a ConsoleColor).
Decorations for the whole text: Bold, Dim, Italic, Underline, Strikethrough, Invert.

The encoding of a new log file: utf8 without a byte order mark by default (Write-Color defaults to unicode, which is UTF-16 LE); Write-Color's names mean the same here (unicode, string and unknown are UTF-16 LE, bigendianunicode UTF-16 BE, utf32 UTF-32 LE), plus utf8BOM and utf8NoBOM. Appending to an existing file always keeps that file's encoding (detected from its byte order mark, or UTF-16 text without one), so a UTF-16 log from Write-Color stays UTF-16; when -Encoding names a different one, a warning says so.
Two colours: the text is coloured from the first to the second (per character; steps on 16-colour terminals).
Centres each line in the window (measured in terminal cells, so emoji and CJK centre correctly).
A level for the log record (Info, Warning, Error...).
Empty lines after the text.
Empty lines before the text.
A hyperlink target for the whole text (OSC 8 where supported).
A log file the text is appended to (plain text, see -LogFormat).
The log format: Text (the Write-Color layout), Csv or JsonLines.
Attempts to write the log file before giving up with a warning (default 2).
The CSV separator (default a comma).
Whether log lines start with the time (default $true).
Markup added after the pieces ([bold lime]Ready[/] in [muted]3s[/]).
Writes only to the log file.
Leaves the line open, so the next output continues on it.
Centres the text within this many cells.
The padding character (default a space).
Pads the text on the left to this many cells (right-aligned).
Pads the text on the right to this many cells.
A theme role for pieces without their own colour (Pass, Fail, Warn, Info, Muted, Accent...).
Starts the line with the time in brackets.
Splits the text at this separator; the following lines are aligned under the first, after the time and prefix.
Spaces before the text.
Tabs before the text (eight cells each).
Text pieces, shown literally (strings, or rich text from New-ConsoleText).
The time format for -ShowTimestamp and the log (default yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss).
The width for -Wrap and -HorizontalCenter (default the window width).
Wraps long text at the window width, continuing under the text after the time and prefix.
